issues.legal_issue: The legal effect of annual feeding and a contingent educational surplus on the characterization of a perpetual dedication primarily connected with worship at a tomb.
material_facts: The settlement charged the endowed properties solely with services connected with the deceased person's tomb, including daily worship and annual ceremonies there.
Annual feeding was provided for as part of the ceremonies at the tomb; the deed described the feeding and other services as connected with the tomb's upkeep and worship.
Education was to receive only any surplus remaining after the tomb-related expenses, and that surplus depended on the manager's choice of how much to spend on those services.
issues.conclusion: The dominant purpose of the dedication was worship of and at the tomb; the annual feeding and contingent educational surplus did not make it a dedication for other religious or charitable purposes.
issues.legal_principle: The purpose of a dedication is determined from the deed as a whole and its dominant motive. Incidental or dependent uses do not displace the dominant purpose. The Court accordingly treated the feeding as part of the tomb-related worship and the educational use as contingent and indefinite.

rule.if: perpetual_endowment_dispute and tomb_worship_is_stated_primary_purpose and (feeding_is_tied_to_tomb_rituals or education_is_only_contingent_surplus)

predicates.perpetual_endowment_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a perpetual dedication of property for religious or charitable purposes is valid.
predicates.tomb_worship_is_stated_primary_purpose: The dedication instrument charges property primarily with services connected with worship at a deceased person's tomb.
predicates.feeding_is_tied_to_tomb_rituals: The instrument provides for feeding as part of ceremonies connected with worship at the tomb.
predicates.education_is_only_contingent_surplus: The instrument directs only an uncertain surplus, left after the tomb-related expenses, to educational purposes.

issues.definition: When a perpetual endowment dispute concerns a dedication primarily for tomb worship and feeding is tied to its rituals or education is only a contingent surplus use, those ancillary uses do not change the dominant purpose.

issues.legal_issue: The validity under Hindu law of a perpetual dedication primarily for worship at the tomb of an ordinary deceased person.
material_facts: The settlement permanently dedicated properties to services connected with the deceased person's tomb, including daily worship and annual ceremonies.
The deed's other stated purposes were part of the tomb-related services or dependent on a surplus after their expenses.
There was no evidence that the community concerned had a widely recognized practice of making such endowments; the pleadings asserted that tomb ceremonies were not usual in that community.
issues.conclusion: A perpetual dedication primarily for worship at the tomb was invalid under Hindu law, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A perpetual dedication can escape the rule against perpetuity only if it is for a religious or charitable purpose recognized by Hindu law. Where religious merit is relied on without public benefit, the purpose must have a Shastric basis; a later practice may also qualify if it has wide recognition among a substantial class. The Court approved Kunhamutty v. Thondikkodan Ahmad Musaliar, A. Draviasundaram Pillai v. N. Subramania Pillai, and Veluswami Goundan v. Dandapani, which rejected perpetual endowments for tomb worship. It distinguished M. K. A. Ramanathan Chettiar v. Vada Levvai Marakayar, concerning Muslims, and Board of Commissioners for Hindu Religious Endowments v. Pidugu Narasimham, concerning public worship of installed images and a sovereign grant. It also referred to Fatma Bibi v. Advocate-General of Bombay, Dwarakanath Bysack v. Burroda Persaud Bysack, Rupa Jagashet v. Krishnaji, and Parthasarthy Pillai v. Thiruvengada Pillai in discussing Hindu religious purposes and religious merit.

rule.if: perpetual_endowment_validity_dispute and tomb_worship_is_dominant_purpose and no_shastric_basis_is_shown and no_widely_recognized_practice_is_shown

predicates.perpetual_endowment_validity_dispute: The proceeding concerns the validity of a perpetual dedication of property for a religious or charitable purpose.
predicates.tomb_worship_is_dominant_purpose: The endowed property is primarily devoted to worship of or at the tomb of a deceased person.
predicates.no_shastric_basis_is_shown: No basis in Hindu sacred texts is shown for treating the purpose as one that produces religious merit.
predicates.no_widely_recognized_practice_is_shown: No widely recognized practice among a substantial class is shown to support the purpose as religious.

issues.definition: When a perpetual endowment validity dispute concerns a dedication primarily for tomb worship and neither a Shastric basis nor a widely recognized practice is shown, the endowment is invalid.
